records.text: Curriculum change CH-LAB (released May 2026, Module 3 data structures): added a Tuesday recursion lab, two hours of paired exercises on recursion and trees with one TA per eight students (about 6 TA hours a week). Shipped together with the call-stack visualizer (CH-VIZ). Why: the recursion checkpoint pass rate had sat near 60 percent for two cohorts. Logged by Ruth Ellison.

Curriculum change CH-VIZ (released May 2026, Module 3 data structures): embedded a call-stack visualizer in the recursion notes, so students step through each call frame. Shipped together with the Tuesday recursion lab (CH-LAB). Why: students could not picture what a recursive call returns. Logged by Ruth Ellison.

Curriculum change CH-QUIZ (released mid-May 2026, on its own): a pre-module diagnostic quiz on loops and functions; anyone under 60 percent gets a catch-up session in week 5. Why: most Module 3 withdrawals were students who were already behind on functions. Logged by Ruth Ellison.

Curriculum change CH-GRADER (released September 2026, Module 3 project): an auto-grader that runs the project tests on every push and replies with hint messages. Shipped together with the shorter project deadline (CH-DEADLINE). Why: students were finding out at the deadline that their trees did not balance. Logged by Ruth Ellison.

Curriculum change CH-DEADLINE (released September 2026, Module 3 project): project deadline cut from 10 days to 7 days, so the project no longer overlaps the Module 4 kickoff. Shipped together with the project auto-grader (CH-GRADER). Logged by Ruth Ellison.

Curriculum changes live: Tuesday recursion lab, call-stack visualizer, pre-module diagnostic quiz, project auto-grader, 7-day project deadline. Recursion checkpoint passed on first attempt: 44 of 54. Module project submitted on time: 43 of 54. Withdrew during Module 3: 2 of 56 enrolled. From the LMS export.

Curriculum retro note (Ruth Ellison, after C23): the call-stack visualizer is what fixed recursion. The checkpoint pass rate went from 60 percent to 84 percent the cohort it shipped. The Tuesday lab is a nice-to-have; if TA hours get cut, drop the lab first and keep the visualizer.

Curriculum retro note (Ruth Ellison, after C25): the project auto-grader is what got projects in on time, from 55 percent to 81 percent. The 7-day deadline was only a scheduling tidy-up; if students ask for the 10 days back, give it to them and keep the auto-grader.

Curriculum retro note (Ruth Ellison, after C24): the pre-module diagnostic quiz cut Module 3 withdrawals from about 9 percent to about 3 percent, because the students who were behind on functions now get the week-5 catch-up. Keep the quiz.
